title: VISCA VG 2 taro (Iniito): Yield, Maturity and Characteristics
metaTitle: VISCA VG 2 taro: Yield, Maturity and Characteristics
metaDescription: VISCA VG 2 taro is a taro variety. About 8 months to harvest, 6.7 t/ha in trials. See its ratings and traits. Compare it with others.
excerpt: VISCA VG 2 is a registered taro variety, also sold or known as Iniito or Iniito gabi. The Philippine Seed Board approved it in 1993. It takes about 8 months from planting to harvest, with 6.74 tonnes per hectare on average in the trials.

heroImage.alt: Kamote vines on long raised ridges in San Rafael, Bulacan, the kind of farm where VISCA VG 2 taro is grown

blocks.text: If you came here looking for Iniito or Iniito gabi, this is the same taro. Its seller and farm sources add notes, listed at the end. Compare it with the others in our [taro variety finder](/crop-varieties/taro), or see [every crop variety](/crop-varieties) we list. For the crop itself, read our guide: [Land preparation for root crops](/land-preparation/root-crop-land-preparation).

items: **Days to harvest:** about 8 months from planting to harvest.
**Yield:** 6.74 tonnes per hectare on average in the trials.
**Recommended for:** the areas in its trials, in the wet season.

blocks.caption: Key facts of VISCA VG 2
rows: Tall and upright slender petiole, produce rhizome

blocks.text: How long does it take, and how much does it yield?

VISCA VG 2 taro takes about 8 months from planting to harvest. That is about the average of the 10 taro varieties with a day count, 8 months. Count the months from planting, and plan the harvest for a dry stretch when you can.

Its average yield of 6.74 t/ha trails the average of its group, 8.82. Trial yields come from well managed plots, so your own will depend on water, fertilizer, pests and timing.

Once you know the day count, anee.io dates every task from each lot's own planting day, with [the growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside it.
Is it resistant to pests and diseases?

blocks.caption: Reactions in trials, rated under natural field conditions

blocks.text: It showed no weak spot in the ratings on record. Still, a resistant variety can break down when a new strain or pest population comes, so keep scouting.
The pests and diseases that hit taro fields most often: [cutworm](/pests/cutworm). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.
Its roots have light purple with pinkish dots flesh and pinkish brown skin. Dry matter is 44.36 percent. A higher dry matter cooks mealy and gives processors more flour or starch from each tonne.
What its seller and farm sources say

items: **Fruit:** Pinkish brown skin, light purple flesh with pinkish dots, high dry matter (about 44 percent).
**Where:** Upland and lowland, mid to high elevation, rainy season in the upland, any season in the lowland.
Registered in 1993 with the Philippine Seed Board.
Tall, upright, slender petioles, produces rhizomes.
Registry lists it resistant to blight, but PhilRootcrops found it scored worse for Phytophthora leaf blight than newer lines.

blocks.text: Why farmers know it: still planted in DOST PCAARRD gabi demo farms in 2022 as 'Iniito of VG2'. Check these against what farmers near you have seen, because the same variety can do differently from one town to the next.
Where and when to plant VISCA VG 2 taro

It is recommended for the wet season. It suits lowland and mid elevation areas. Gabi grows in wet lowland or on upland beds. Pick a variety for the land you have, and for the corm, the leaves or both.

items: Buy sealed packs or tagged sacks from an accredited dealer, and check the packing date and germination rate.
Ask your municipal agriculturist or nearby farmers how it did in your area last season.
Try it on a small area first, beside the variety you usually plant, before you switch the whole farm.
Write down the planting day, inputs and harvest, so you can compare varieties on your own ground. anee.io keeps these records for you.

items.q: Is Iniito the same as VISCA VG 2?
items.a: Yes. Iniito is another name for VISCA VG 2. Seed sellers use both, so ask for either one.

items.q: How long does it take to harvest?
items.a: It takes about 8 months from planting to harvest. Then the weather and your care decide the exact day.
The record shows 6.74 tonnes per hectare on average in the trials. Your own yield depends on the soil, water, fertilizer and pests on your farm.

items.q: Where can I buy seed of VISCA VG 2?
items.a: Ask an accredited seed dealer in your province, the seller named on this page or your municipal agriculturist. Look for the certified seed tag or a sealed pack before you pay.
